guide: Open Start here and type your names, the wedding day, the seated capacity from the venue contract and the seats at one table in the yellow cells. Replace demo data: clear the sample rows and type your own.
Fill Households and Guests first: one row per invitation and one per guest with side, tier, list, RSVP, meal and a short dietary note. Names only, no addresses and no health details.
Type the seats of each table in Seating Tables. The seated guests, the free seats and the side mix fill in as you type a table for each guest in Guests.
Check the room first: Capacity Scenarios, the Table Count Solver, the Table Size Comparison and the Floor Space Check say whether the guests fit before you seat anyone.
Add Seat Rules (keep together or keep apart, with a short reason). Rule Conflicts and Seat Swaps list what to fix and the Keep Together Apart Checker counts it.
Seat the yes guests with no table from Unseated Guests, then use the Late Reply Seat Tool for each late yes. Spare Seat Reserve shows the seats to hold for pending replies.
Look at Table Fill and Table Balance by Side and Tier for tables that are full or all one side, and at the Household Split Check so children sit with their household.
Type the rental items in Rental Quantities; the quantity comes from the final tables with your spare share. Send the Rental Order Page to the rentals vendor.
Print the Place Cards, the Head Table Plan and the table signs, then run the Final Seating Sign-off. Ready to print means every check is clear.
Use the 18 tools, print 12 sheets and 12 pages, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
A couple with a small wedding (30 guests, no wedding party) uses the same sheets with fewer rows: keep one or two tables, skip the head table or the whole seating plan.
This workbook has no macros and works in Excel and Google Sheets. Print any page for a parent or the day-of coordinator.
Why a workbook: one flat price, no vendor ever sees your details, no fees on your gifts, your own numbers, and it works offline.
What this is not: not a booking service, not a payment service, and not legal, tax or insurance advice. Every default is a typical starting value you can edit, never a promise.

listing.headline: Seating chart, table count and venue capacity for your wedding
listing.description:
Plan where every guest sits in one Excel workbook. Built for an engaged couple planning their own wedding, with a parent, a wedding party lead or the day-of coordinator helping with the room. Guests and Households hold one row per guest and one per invitation (one invitation, several people) with side, tier, RSVP and meal. Names only: no addresses and no health details.

Start with the room. The Table Count Solver turns the headcount plus the couple, vendor and spare seats into tables and tells you if you fit; the Table Size Comparison picks between tables of 6, 8, 10 and 12; the Everyone Says Yes Scenario shows how many seats over you are if every invited guest comes; the Floor Space Check shares the floor area among your guests after the dance floor, buffet and stage.

Then seat. Seat Rules hold the keep-together and keep-apart pairs with a short reason; the Keep Together Apart Checker lists every conflict and the Seat Swap Suggester names the move or the swap. The Late Reply Seat Tool finds the table with room that fits the side of a late yes, Table Fill and Table Balance show full and one-sided tables, and the Household Split Check keeps children with their household.

Finish with the paper. Rental Quantities gives chairs, linens, plates and glasses from the final tables with your spare share, Place Cards and the Head Table Plan print for the day, and the Final Seating Sign-off gives a print date and says what is left.

18 tools answer weekly questions. Print 12 sheets and 12 pages, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to guests, the venue, the caterer, the rentals vendor and your helpers. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Every default is a typical starting value you can edit and forecasts are your own estimate. It is not a booking service, not a payment service and not legal, tax or insurance advice. This is part five of the Wedding Planning suite.

ar.Colours: cream-yellow cells, and the whi: الألوان: الخلايا الصفراء الفاتحة والأعمدة البيضاء في الجداول هي التي تكتب فيها، أما الخلايا الرمادية المزرقة الفاتحة فتُحسب لك تلقائياً.
ar.Protection: every sheet is protected, wi: الحماية: كل ورقة محمية بلا كلمة مرور حتى لا تُمسح المعادلات بالخطأ. الخلايا المحسوبة مقفلة، وكل خلية مخصصة لإدخالك تبقى مفتوحة.
ar.To change something that is locked: Revi: لتعديل شيء مقفل: مراجعة > إلغاء حماية الورقة (لا حاجة إلى كلمة مرور)، ويمكنك حماية الورقة مجدداً بعد ذلك إن أردت.
ar.Currency symbol: type it once in the \"C: رمز العملة: اكتبه مرة واحدة في خانة «رمز العملة» ضمن الإعدادات أدناه (الافتراضي $). يظهر في المبالغ المكتوبة داخل النصوص وبجانب المبالغ في لوحة المؤشرات والأدوات.
ar.Dates: date cells follow your computer's: التواريخ: خلايا التاريخ تتبع التنسيق الإقليمي لجهازك (مثل DD/MM/YYYY أو MM/DD/YYYY)، أما التواريخ المكتوبة داخل النصوص (المستندات والرسائل) فتتبع خانة «تنسيق التاريخ» ضمن الإعدادات أدناه.
ar.Google Sheets: upload this file to Googl: Google Sheets: ارفع هذا الملف إلى Google Drive وافتحه باستخدام Google Sheets؛ كل شيء يُحسب هناك أيضاً. قفل الأوراق لا ينتقل إلى Google Sheets، لذا اكتب في خلايا الإدخال فقط.
